subject: Private deployment routing guardrails and PoC decision matrix
messages:
From: Sumit Rao <s.rao@archway.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — initial network questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. A quick recap from our side and a couple of concrete asks so we can scope the PoC: 

- Our workload: real-time inference for user chat with streaming token output; expected steady-state concurrency ~60 simultaneous streams, peak bursts to ~120 for short windows.
- Desired SLOs (what we'd like to validate): p95 token latency < 180ms, tail (p99) < 350ms for streaming responses; throughput target ~12k tokens/sec aggregate across the private cluster.
- Network setup: we'll be behind an IPSEC VPN to Redwood private peering; egress will go through our transit VPC (single egress IP set).

Two asks before we lock a test window:
1) What are Redwood's recommended tunnel settings (MTU, keep-alive, encryption profile) for streaming workloads?
2) Any standard smoke test script you want us to run from our side (traceroute, iperf, tcpdump) so results are comparable?

I attached a simple network diagram for context.

If helpful, we can target a two-hour PoC window the week of Mar 8 — let me know availability.

Thanks,
Sumit Rao
Head of Platform & Ops
Archway AI

Subject: Re: Private deployment — initial network questions

Sumit — thanks for the clear summary and diagram. Following up with a concise post-call decision matrix and next steps so everyone has the same playbook. High-level notes first, then asks.

Redwood recommendations (short):
- Target SLOs to validate during PoC: p95 token latency <= 150–180ms (we can align to 150ms if you want an aggressive baseline), p99 streaming tail <= 300–350ms.
- Concurrency and throughput: our Dedicated private runtime can sustain the steady 60 concurrency without special config; for peak bursts to 120 we recommend enabling burst capacity and performing a short soak test.
- VPN/peering: IPSEC with MTU 1400–1412 is recommended; keep-alive UDP 15s, rekey interval 1h. AES-GCM profiles are fine.

Concrete asks from the Archway side before PoC: 
1) Please share a traceroute and one iperf3 run (client->Redwood edge) from your egress colo so we can baseline hop counts and bottlenecks.
2) Provide the public egress IP(s) or a CIDR for firewall rules.
3) Add our test JWK (we'll need a test API key) to your allowlist once we confirm the IPs.

Planned PoC scope (what Redwood will validate in the two-hour window):
- Connectivity validation: IPSEC tunnel health, MTU checks, and path MTU discovery.
- Streaming smoke: 5 parallel streams for 30s, ramp to 60 concurrent, then 2-minute burst to 120. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and per-token latency traces.
- Egress throughput: short iperf-style bursts to verify sustained tokens/sec capacity.

Attachments: I've attached our SLO acceptance template to make the pass/fail criteria explicit.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You run traceroute + iperf3 and share results (action: Sumit).
- We provision a test model and schedule a 2-hour test window Mar 9 or Mar 10 (action: Marissa/Ben).
- Karthik will provide the detailed runbook and a short script for archway to run locally.

If that works, I'll lock Mar 9 13:00–15:00 PT for the PoC and send calendar invites.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in some low-level test details we'll run on the Redwood edge side. High-level test checklist and recommended tunnel params: 

Edge checklist (Redwood):
- Verify IPSEC SA lifetime and rekey behavior under concurrent streams.
- Confirm NAT traversal and packet size behavior — ensure PMTU black hole tests pass.
- Capture pcap for the first 2 minutes of the PoC for diagnostics (we will sanitize and share offsets).

Recommended tunnel settings: 
- MTU: 1412 (accounts for encryption overhead on common IPSec configs).
- Keep-alive: 15s, Rekey: 3600s.
- Ports: ensure UDP 4500 and ESP are open; allow ephemeral UDP 49152–65535 for NAT-T flows.

Short test script we'll run from Redwood:
1) Baseline RTT and hop counts (3 traceroute passes).
2) Single stream 60s streaming check (p50/p95/p99).
3) Ramp test: 5 -> 60 -> 120 concurrency with 30s holds at each step.
4) Short egress saturation: 2x 60s iperf bursts to measure tokens/sec equivalent (we'll provide mapping).

Attachment: small helper script I use for egress sanity checks.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment — PoC runbook and acceptance criteria

Sumit — following Marissa and Ben's notes, here's a compact runbook and pass/fail matrix you can use to sign off the PoC. Please paste this into your tracking doc so the network and platform teams share the same expectations.

PoC runbook (2-hour window):
- Phase 0 (15m): Tunnel bring-up and MTU verification (traceroute + PMTU). PASS = no fragmentation observed; ICMP blackhole < 1 per 1k packets.
- Phase 1 (25m): Baseline single-stream sample. Measure p50/p95/p99 for 20 sample responses. PASS = p95 <= 180ms.
- Phase 2 (40m): Steady-state concurrency 60 for 15m; collect token-level latencies. PASS = p95 <= 180ms and no >5% request failures.
- Phase 3 (25m): Burst to 120 for 5m, observe tail behavior and failover to burst capacity. PASS = degradation < 2x p95 and graceful shedding if overload.
- Phase 4 (15m): Egress throughput bursts and teardown. PASS = sustained tokens/sec within +/-10% of expected.

Action items and owners: 
- Archway: run traceroute + iperf3 and share results by EOD Mar 6. (owner: Sumit)
- Redwood infra: provision test model, reserve burst capacity, and pre-stage pcap capture. (owner: Ben)
- Redwood network: produce ephemeral allowlist and test IPs, confirm UDP/ESP reachability. (owner: Laura)
- Both: agree on exact test timestamps and test API key rotation plan. (owner: Marissa)

Checklist for Archway network team to provide with traceroute/iperf: 
- Public egress IP(s) or CIDR; sample traceroute output (3 runs); iperf3 -c <redwood-edge> 2x 60s runs.
- Config snippet for IPSEC (proposal: any standard AES-GCM profile) and whether you have an existing NAT device that could rewrite UDP source ports.

If all that is fine I confirm Mar 9 13:00–15:00 PT for the PoC. I'll upload a short runbook to the shared Drive and paste the link below.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
